title: Champion Swimmer Archie Goodburn to Carry the Match Ball Before 60,000 Fans
summary:
A champion swimmer is about to have one of the biggest moments of his life — and it won't be in a pool. Archie Goodburn, a 25-year-old swimmer from Edinburgh, will deliver the match ball for Scotland's rugby game against Australia at Murrayfield stadium next month, in front of more than 60,000 fans.

Goodburn is the Scottish record holder for the 50-metre breaststroke and a European bronze medallist. But his story is about much more than swimming. In 2024, he was diagnosed with a rare brain tumour. After surgery, he fought his way back into competitive swimming — and he also started campaigning so that other people with brain cancer can get better treatment and more research. In recent weeks he has taken that campaign to Prime Minister Andy Burnham and to Scotland's First Minister, John Swinney.

Before swimming took over, Goodburn played rugby as a blindside flanker at school, so carrying the ball onto the pitch at Murrayfield — in his home city — is a perfect fit. “This means the absolute world to me,” he said. The biggest crowd he has ever performed for was 10,000 people at the Edinburgh Military Tattoo, where he sang a solo of “What a Wonderful World” at age 12. This time the audience will be six times bigger.

The match takes place on Sunday, November 15, and supporters at the stadium will be able to donate to two charities, Brain Tumour Research and the Astro Brain Tumour Fund. Goodburn believes moments like this can help: “Things are beginning to move and this kind of initiative can make a difference.”
why_it_matters: Goodburn's appearance links a major sporting event to health research, showing how one public moment can bring attention and donations to brain tumour treatment. It also shows an athlete rebuilding his career after serious illness.

keywords.explanation: Breaststroke is a swimming stroke swum on your front with both arms moving together.
A medallist is a person who has won a medal in a competition.
A tumour is an abnormal growth in the body that can make a person seriously ill.
Campaigning means working publicly to persuade people in power to make a change.
A blindside flanker is a rugby position on the side of the scrum the ball carrier cannot easily see.

background_read: Delivering the match ball is a ceremonial honour in rugby, where a special guest carries the ball onto the pitch before the game begins.
Murrayfield is Scotland's home rugby stadium in Edinburgh, so a Scottish athlete can be honoured there in front of a home crowd.
Goodburn's main swimming event is the 50-metre breaststroke, a short sprint race swum on the front.
Charities raise money to study illnesses and improve treatment, which is why a public moment at a big match can help a campaign reach many people.
